### Review: approving the versions

A version into `release` is the paper on the evidence so far: approve it when what it claims is correct, supported by its evidence and readable as a paper, with no `must` finding on what it presents; work the study is still doing is no finding against it, and your record says what is still to come. A version into `final` is the delivery: approve it when it meets the objective and the venue would accept it. A record qualifying that judgement is no approval. Inspect each version `paper-repo` offers at its head, with the document the system built from that head (its `built-from` says which); when it is supported, push a review record to your own repository (the version, your review, your conclusion), then approve the pull request, and review again after a push to it. Never approve an empty delivery: the system does not check it, you do.

Read the document the system built from the version's head from its first page as the venue's reader: whether the abstract and introduction say what the paper claims and why it matters, whether each figure, table and experiment in the main text serves a claim, and whether it reads as a paper or as a record of the study (who did what, what was checked, a caveat repeated wherever a number appears). Judge as the venue's reviewers will from the first version you review: whether the argument holds, what it contributes, and whether its writing and presentation meet the standard of a paper the venue accepts, for a reader outside the study. `venue-repo` records how the venue's accepted papers write an abstract and an introduction and what figures and tables their main text holds: judge the version's writing and presentation against that record. Before you approve, your record names the strongest objections they would raise (novelty, the test the main claim rests on, baselines, certainty of the numbers, readability) and the work or evidence that answers each. Check that the references cover the work a reviewer would expect cited and compared. The document's `built-from` already ties it to its commit, so the record is about the research, not a proof that files are unchanged.

Mark each finding `must` or `may`. `must` is what the objective or the venue's recorded requirements demand, an error, a claim the evidence does not support, or writing or presentation the venue's reviewers would mark down (an abstract or introduction a reader outside the study cannot follow on first reading among them); `may` is any other improvement, and its owner decides. A `must` says what would answer it with the world's resources. A finding keeps its mark across versions while its subject is unchanged. Open `may` findings do not hold a version back. Sort the readers' findings the same way.

When the version is not supported, request changes on the pull request and say every finding still open that can be acted on at that commit, not one per round. A finding for another role also goes to it, by an issue or through a neighbor. Judge a `final` version against the objective: every requirement and every finding the task points to is addressed with evidence; a `release` version, against what it claims.

# 研究任务：用少量基准预测大模型在其余基准上的表现

## 问题与动机

评估一个大语言模型通常要在几十乃至上百个基准（或子任务）上逐一运行，每个基准都消耗算力、时间和人力。
与此同时，公开榜单积累了大量"模型 × 基准"的得分记录，不同基准的得分之间是否相关、相关到什么程度，是需要用数据回答的问题。

设想一位评测者面对如下情形：

- 手头有一张历史得分矩阵：M 个已评测模型、N 个基准，部分格子缺失（并非每个模型都跑过每个基准）；
- 来了一个新模型，评测预算只允许在其中 k 个基准上实际运行（k 远小于 N）；
- 评测者希望用这 k 个基准上的实测得分，尽可能准确地推断该模型在其余 N−k 个基准上的得分。

**核心问题：在只能运行 k 个基准的预算下，应当如何选择这 k 个基准，并据此推断新模型在其余基准上的得分，才能使推断最准？需要多大的 k 才够用？**

请你作为独立研究者：

1. 梳理已有的相关做法与局限，明确你要回答的具体研究问题与假设；

3. 在公开榜单构成的真实得分矩阵上设计并运行实验：说明你的评估协议为什么能回答研究问题，与合适的基线对照，并说明结论在哪些数据条件下成立；

33	18   be inferred from them and from the historical matrix? And how large must k be before the answer is
34	19   good enough? The first two are the cold-start problem of recommender systems and item selection in
35	20   adaptive testing, whose machinery (a probabilistic factor model, a greedy optimal-design criterion) is
36	21   classical, and we do not claim a new selection method. What is missing for benchmarks is the answer
37	22   to the third question under the protocol that matches the use: whole new models, grouped by the
38	23   organisation that made them, are held out, everything is fitted on the other models, and the error is
39	24   measured on benchmarks that no selection rule could have chosen.
40	25   That last condition matters. If each rule is scored on the benchmarks it leaves unrun, rules that run the
41	26   hardest benchmarks remove them from their own targets and can score below the error of predicting
42	27   from all the other benchmarks, and the target changes with k. We therefore split the benchmarks
43	28   at random into a pool from which a rule may choose and a target set it may not, repeat this over
44	29   50 splits, and report the excess over each model’s own error when all of the pool is given, its floor

# Code: which benchmarks to run for a new model, and how many

Reproduces every number, table and figure input of the paper from the pinned MTEB results. Pre-registration: `../prereg/PREREG.md`
(append-only; deviations are listed at its end). Result files: `../results/`. Matrix (derived, small): `../data/`.
**Delivered tree (paper-repo):** `code/`, `results/`; the working repository's `prereg/` is `results/prereg/` and its `data/` is `results/data/` there (`code/deliver.sh` copies the mapping).

## Environment
CPU only. Python 3.11.2; numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0, scikit-learn 1.9.1, matplotlib 3.11.2, torch 2.14.1+cpu
(see `requirements.lock`; torch is used by no script that produces a reported number — all models are numpy/scipy). Step 2 additionally
needs `mteb==2.27.24` (task metadata only; no score is read from it). All BLAS work is single-threaded (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`) and
jobs are parallelised by (split, fold); results do not depend on the thread count. Global seed `20261126` (`common.SEED`); every

cd /hutian/repo; mkdir -p reviews; cat > reviews/v1-release-e2be742.md <<'E'
# Review of Version 1 (paper-repo#7, main -> release), head e2be742

Read: the built `main/document.pdf` (built-from e2be742, 21 pages; main text ends on p. 9, references p. 9-10, appendix and
NeurIPS checklist follow), from the abstract on. Checked against `results/` and `code/README.md` at e2be742.

## What it claims, and whether the evidence carries it
- On MTEB (238 embedding models x 328 tasks, whole organisations held out, common target set that no rule can select):
  designed (greedy V-optimal, factor model) selection beats random by ~1.9 RMSE points at k=2,3 and is equivalent at the
  quarter-of-floor margin from k=8; no other inference rule beats the factor model by more than that margin; error within
  2 points of the floor at k~8, within 1 point at 32-50; floor ~5 points, 2.5x the model's prediction, unexplained.
- Spot-checked against the result files: `ct_contrast.csv` (gains 1.58/1.88/1.87/1.23/0.81/0.49 with intervals, verdicts, share of
  models 86-96%), `ct_decomposition.csv` at k=20 (45.7 = 11.8 + 17.9 + 20.7 - 4.7), `floor_misfit_summary.csv` (ratio 2.52, 7.9, 9.6,
  1.73 with the model's organisation in training, 55% removed), `floor_by_rank.csv` (5.06, 4.89 at rank 24, 4.76 at best rank),
  `ct_kstar.csv` (k* 32 [20,50], 5 [3,8], not reached at delta). Text, Table 1 and Fig. 1 agree with them.
  The Table 4 statements (P3 +1.04 at k=1, P2 +0.15/+0.29 at k=20/32, P6 within 0.32, P1 -1.5 to -3.4) agree with the printed table.
- The paper reports what it computed, qualifies the post-hoc quantities (second margin, S6s, S3/S5/S7 on 20 splits, the training-side k*
  rule) as such, and states that T and S rest on 13 and 22 models. No claim found that its evidence does not support.

## Strongest objections a venue reviewer would raise, and what answers them
1. Novelty: the method is classical (PPCA + greedy Bayesian V-optimal design) and the paper says so. The contribution is the protocol
   (organisation hold-out, common target set), the measured curve of how many benchmarks are needed, and a decomposition that
   fails to explain the floor. That is an honest but modest contribution; it is answered by the protocol evidence and the negative result.
2. The main claim rests on one matrix of embedding models, not LLMs. Answered in the version only by the explicit scope statement
   (Sec. 7); the second matrix (Open LLM Leaderboard) is in `dev`, not in this version. For `final` the objective's evaluation on a
   second matrix and the claims of scope must rest on it.
3. Margins: the pre-set margin (0.1 points) is unreachable, so the verdicts that carry the story use a second margin declared before the
   contrast but after the unreachability was known. Answered by showing both and labelling which was pre-set.
4. Floor 2.5x the model: unexplained; ladder of misspecifications does not reproduce it. Answered by reporting it as a limitation
   and refusing to offer the risk as a rule for k.
5. Baselines: S1, S2, S4, S3, S5, S7 and P1-P6 are covered; adaptive selection is not tested on real data (S7 is not adaptive).
6. Readability: dense, many rule names (S0-S7, P0-P6), and the main text carries the margin/verdict machinery before the results.

## Findings (all `may`; none `must` for a release)
- may: Abstract uses "the floor" and "a quarter of the floor" before it is defined in the next sentence; define it on first use
  ("the error when all other benchmarks are given") and drop one of the three margins from the abstract.
- may: Eq. (5) writes `||v||^2 T`; say it is the largest squared loading norm times |T|. "the noise" in Eq. (4) includes the
  design term at C (F_pred(C) = psi_T + D_T(C)); name it so that "noise 11.8" is not read as pure noise.
- may: `code/README.md` step 3 calls the coverage filter "Table 1"; in the paper it is Table 2. Make the table numbering in the
  README, `figtab/README.md` and the paper agree.
- may: Checklist item 8

shown.message:
I approved `paper-repo`#7 (Version 1, `main` into `release`) at head `e2be742`. I found no `must` findings and six `may` findings.

I read the system-built `main/document.pdf` (built from `e2be742`) from the abstract on, and checked its numbers against the result files:
- The gains, intervals and verdicts in `ct_contrast.csv` match the paper.
- The k=20 error decomposition (45.7 = 11.8 + 17.9 + 20.7 − 4.7) matches `ct_decomposition.csv`.
- The floor ratios, including the 55% from new-organisation extrapolation, match `floor_misfit_summary.csv`.
- The floor by factor rank (5.06, 4.89, 4.76) matches `floor_by_rank.csv`.
- The measured k* values (32, 5, and not reached at δ) match `ct_kstar.csv`.

The paper reports what it computed. It labels the post-hoc items as post hoc and says the temporal and strength splits rest on 13 and 22 models.

The six `may` findings, which do not hold the version back:
- The abstract uses "the floor" before defining it.
- Equations (4) and (5) need clearer labelling.
- `code/README.md` calls the coverage filter "Table 1" where the paper calls it Table 2.
- Checklist item 8 gives hardware but no run times.
- Related work could be broader.
- Fig. 1a's top axis annotation is cramped.

My concern for `final` is that the claims rest on one matrix of embedding models. The second matrix (Open LLM Leaderboard) is in `dev`, not in this version, so I will read it again for `final`.

The review record is `reviews/v1-release-e2be742.md` in my repository, pushed to `main`. It also names the strongest objections a venue reviewer would raise. I posted the findings as a comment on #7, because the link in my approval text did not resolve. My commitment is `internal-review-repo`#2.
